newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Belgium offers cash and back-up for Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Belgium offers cash and back-up for Zaire force.

text.p: Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke has said his country will give cash and logistical backup for a multinational force for Zaire, but would not send troops back into its former colony.

He told a news conference in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa late on Tuesday that Belgium, Zaire's former colonial master, had already contributed 300 million Belgium francs ($10 million) towards a fund to deploy a force.
He was in Ethiopia to sit in on African leaders' talks on Monday on the crisis affecting more than a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees sent fleeing by fighting in east Zaire.
Canada has offered to lead a multinational force to bring aid to the refugees, and says it will need some 10,000 troops for more than two months.

African states have called for a "neutral" force and Derycke said Belgium, which has lost paratroopers in earlier interventions since granting Zaire independence at the start of the 1960s, would not join.
"Belgium had bad experience in this regard and will not do so for obvious reasons," he said.
Derycke, who was returning to Brussels on Wednesday, also said Belgium has dispatched four C-130 planes to Entebbe in Uganda to help transport aid supplies.
